headlines.title: Sen. Cassidy announces he will support Blanche's nomination as attorney general
headlines.description: Sen. Bill Cassidy, R-La., announced he would be supporting Todd Blanche's nomination to serve as attorney general. In his speech on the Senate floor, Cassidy explained his reasoning for the decision and voiced some concerns about the Trump administration's relationship with the Justice Department.

headlines.title: Rep. Andy Ogles loses his Republican primary in Tennessee
headlines.description: Rep. Andy Ogles of Tennessee has lost his Republican primary, NBC News projects, falling to a former state official in a primary season that has seen an unusually high number of incumbents lose renomination.

headlines.title: Sen. Marsha Blackburn wins the Republican primary for governor of Tennessee
headlines.description: Blackburn, a longtime Trump ally, defeated Rep. John Rose for the nomination, NBC News projects, after the president decided not to endorse in the race.

headlines.title: Iran Says Hormuz Deal is Close; Trump Denies Munitions Shortage
headlines.description: Iran and Oman are negotiating on the future control of the Strait of Hormuz, but Iran continues to deny having any recent direct talks with the United States. Meanwhile, President Donald Trump is insisting the U.S. has the capability to return to sustained combat, despite reports of dwindling stockpiles of some key munitions. NBC’s Keir Simmons reports for TODAY.

headlines.title: NBC News speaks with Palestinian in West Bank whose home is surrounded by Israeli settlers
headlines.description: Human rights groups say Israeli settler violence against Palestinians in the West Bank has surged. NBC News' Richard Engel visits one village in the middle of the attacks, speaking with a man who says his house is surrounded by settlers.

headlines.title: School shooting in Thailand leaves multiple dead after student fatally shot grandparents
headlines.description: A 14-year-old student in shot and killed his grandparents before killing others and himself at a school in Thailand. NBC News' Janis Mackey Frayer has details on the incident and early investigation into the suspect.

headlines.title: Spokane Wildfire Suspect Confesses to Setting Dozens of Fires
headlines.description: Aaron Farinacci, the man charged with setting one of the most destructive fires in the history of Washington state, appeared in court on Thursday for his arraignment. According to court documents, detectives say Farinacci confessed to using a weather app to wait for a dry and windy day before starting the fire. Farinacci also claims he ignited 25 other fires near his home between July and August of 2025. NBC’s Morgan Chesky reports for TODAY.

headlines.title: Water industry turns to AI and hackers for help after suspected Iran cyberattacks
headlines.description: For the new initiative, Vanderbilt University researchers will work to create “digital twins” of water system networks.

headlines.title: Are Budget Cuts Behind Recent Outbreaks in Foodborne Illnesses?
headlines.description: The CDC and the FDA are saying the tainted lettuce and jalapeños linked to contaminated food illnesses have been traced to Mexico where 63% of all vegetables imported to the United States are grown. Now, some experts are saying recent budget cuts by the Trump administration could have played a role in the outbreak of those illnesses. NBC’s Anne Thompson reports for TODAY.

headlines.title: Witness video of Madison police killing raises questions of why lethal force was used
headlines.description: Local authorities said that the matter is being investigated and that the officers involved have been placed on administrative leave.

headlines.title: Appeals court blocks Trump’s White House ballroom construction
headlines.description: A federal appeals court affirmed a federal judge’s ruling to block construction of the White House ballroom while allowing below-ground construction to move forward.

headlines.title: Woman who killed husband over two decades ago admits to fatally stabbing firefighter wife
headlines.description: A woman in California admitted on Tuesday that she stabbed her wife to death last year, more than two decades after facing prison time for killing her ex-husband in a similar manner.
